title: DevOps and Cloud Engineer
summary: DevOps and cloud engineers build the pipelines and infrastructure that take code from a laptop to running servers, then keep it deployed, scaled and monitored. It suits students who like Linux, automation and fixing why something broke.

sources.title: How to become a DevOps Engineer – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Linux and the command line
nodes.summary: Servers almost always run Linux. Learn files and permissions, processes, package managers, SSH, logs and the shell, so you can work on a machine with no graphical screen.

resources.title: Introduction to Linux (LFS101) – The Linux Foundation
The Missing Semester of Your CS Education – MIT

nodes.proof: Set up a Linux VM, log in over SSH with a key, create users, and write down how you found and read a service's logs.

sources.title: How to become a DevOps Engineer – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Python scripting and Git
nodes.summary: Automation is the core of the job. Learn one language (Python is a common first pick) well enough to write small tools, and use Git for every change: branches, commits, merges and pull requests.
nodes.proof: A public Git repo with a Python script that automates a real chore, such as cleaning old log files or checking if a website is up.

sources.title: How to become a DevOps Engineer – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Networking basics
nodes.summary: Most outages you debug will be network problems. Understand IP addressing, DNS, TCP vs UDP, HTTP, ports, routing and how load balancers and firewalls fit in.

resources.title: Computer Networks and Internet Protocol – NPTEL (IIT Kharagpur)

nodes.proof: Explain, step by step, what happens when you open a URL, and show the DNS lookup and open ports on your own VM using command-line tools.

sources.title: How to become a DevOps Engineer – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Containers with Docker
nodes.summary: Containers package an app with everything it needs so it runs the same everywhere. Learn to write a Dockerfile, build and share images, and run multi-container apps with Docker Compose.
nodes.proof: Containerise a small web app and its database with Docker Compose, with a README showing one command to start it.

nodes.title: CI/CD pipelines
nodes.summary: CI/CD runs builds, tests and deployments automatically on every push. Start with GitHub Actions: triggers, jobs, secrets and building a Docker image in a pipeline.

resources.title: Quickstart for GitHub Actions – GitHub Docs

nodes.proof: A repo where every push runs tests and builds a Docker image, and a failing test blocks the merge.

sources.title: How to become a DevOps Engineer – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: One cloud provider
nodes.summary: Pick one cloud and learn its basics: compute, storage, networking (VPCs), identity and access, and billing. roadmap.sh suggests AWS for beginners; Azure and Google Cloud teach the same ideas.

resources.title: Introduction to Cloud Infrastructure: Apply Azure Skills in Guided Projects – Microsoft Learn

nodes.proof: Host a static site and one small VM on a cloud free tier, set a billing alert, and delete everything afterwards.

sources.title: How to become a DevOps Engineer – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Infrastructure as code with Terraform
nodes.summary: Instead of clicking in a console, describe servers and networks in code so they can be reviewed, repeated and destroyed safely. Learn Terraform's plan/apply cycle, variables, outputs and modules.

resources.title: Get Started – AWS (Terraform tutorials) – HashiCorp Developer

nodes.proof: A Terraform repo that creates and destroys a VM with its network and security group in one command.

sources.title: How to become a DevOps Engineer – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Kubernetes basics
nodes.summary: Kubernetes runs and scales containers across many machines and is asked about in most DevOps interviews. Learn pods, deployments, services, scaling and rolling updates on a local minikube cluster.
nodes.proof: Deploy your containerised app to minikube, scale it to three replicas, and roll out a new version with no downtime.

nodes.title: Project: end-to-end deployment with monitoring
nodes.summary: Tie it all together in one portfolio project: code in Git, CI that tests and builds an image, infrastructure from Terraform or Kubernetes manifests, and Prometheus plus Grafana dashboards watching it.

resources.title: Get started with Grafana and Prometheus – Grafana Docs

nodes.proof: A public repo with an architecture diagram, a pipeline badge, a dashboard screenshot, and a write-up of one problem you hit and fixed.

nodes.title: Interview preparation and job search
nodes.summary: Practise explaining containers vs VMs, CI/CD design, deployment strategies (blue-green, canary) and how you debug incidents, using your own project as examples. An entry cloud certificate is optional; check the official page.
nodes.proof: Answer 20 common DevOps questions out loud in a mock interview, and walk an interviewer through your project's pipeline in five minutes.
